chunks: Al-Bazanti narrated from Dawood ibn Sirhan, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Concerning two men who testified against a man regarding a matter, then two others came and testified to something other than that to which the first two had testified, he said: “Lots are drawn between them; whichever of them is selected by lot, upon him is the oath, and he has greater right to the judgment.”

key_terms.الْيَمِينُ: the oath required in the judicial process
key_terms.يُقْرَعُ: lots are drawn to determine precedence

ai.seo_question: How is judgment made when two sets of witnesses give conflicting testimony in a case?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a judicial dispute in which two pairs of witnesses give conflicting testimony about the same matter. It states that a lot is drawn between them, and the side selected then swears an oath and is given precedence in judgment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3394 - Al-Bazanti narrated from Dawood ibn Sirhan, who said that Abu Abdillah (as) said:

"In the case of two men who testified against another man regarding a matter, and then two others came and testified to something different from what the first two had testified-lots are drawn between them. Whichever group's lot is drawn, they shall take an oath, and their testimony will have precedence in judgment."
